sp.p: Yeah, uh-huh. I'd do it again in a minute, in a heartbeat. And the CO was a millionaire from Hawaii. He was regular army. And his mother owned the controlling interest of Dole Pineapple Company in Hawaii. And he was an infantry officer and he was a fine officer. Name was Barry Rueben. He was a fine, fine officer.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: Now, you had briefly gone into it, you said you go through, was it in '62 when they said you had to go to jump training?

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: No, it was '62.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: '62. I mean, you spend the rest of the time in the service, and then in '62, why did they want you to go to jump training?

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: Well, I had to go with that division. I was a nuclear weapons officer for the Airborne Division in Fort Campbell, Kentucky, and I was the custodian and responsible for the nuclear weapons they took with them if they went to war. And so I had to have jump training. Everybody in the division did.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: So you decided to retire --

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: If I hadn't had 20 years service I would have had to go to jump training.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: Right. So you retired at that time?

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: Yes. I was holding the hold card.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: Okay. And then what did you do after you retired, after retirement?

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: I fished for a while. {Laughter} I went into real estate, and I just hit it lucky. I was with a firm, well-known firm with about 18, 19 salesmen. And I became salesman of the year the first year.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: Where were you living at this time?

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: In Atlanta.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: Okay. How did you end up living in Atlanta?

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: I had a friend that I had known when I was a boy there in Knoxville when I went into the army, and met him in the army, met him again over in Korea, and he told me to come to Atlanta. He asked me if I would like to come live there and I said yeah. And he said, I'll find you a house. So he did, he rented a house for me. I retired and moved in it.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: Now, did you ever go back and visit any of the places where you had served while you were -- after you got out of the army? I know you were over there ___+, but did you ever go after you retired?

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: No, no, I didn't. If I went back it would probably be somewhere like Casablanca. But the only place I've ever visited that I served was my daughter took me out to Fort Oglethorpe to see the little museum they started out there. And of course I was inducted there. I told her, I said, I might have mowed that grass right there.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: {Laughter} Now, what about, you had -- you said after you had come back from the war and then you traveled around, and then you said you were in Germany. Did you go -- did you miss the Berlin Wall at that time or did you see it.

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: No, I didn't see it, but it sure caused us a lot of trouble. They had an all-out alert over there, and they took some of our units that we supported, they were Honest John rocket units and Nike Hercules units, these were all nuclear weapons of any degree of tonnage you want; ten-ton, kiloton, 20-kiloton, whatever. And the Nike, of course, was capable of air bursts and so forth. But anyhow, they put the rockets up where they could be used if the Russians came across the DMZ. That's not the right word, DMZ. Anyhow, came into the American air.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: That is the DMZ in there, isn't it?

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: The DMZ, I think most people think of it as Korea.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: Korea, right.

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: But anyhow, we had these weapons up there on line, and these were armed war reserve weapons. I don't think the country will ever know how close we came to a nuclear war. But anyhow, we had some malfunctions up there. And there was some big thing at the officer's club one night when we were all in dress blues, we had our wives with us and so forth. And they had an alert up there. They had a Nike Hercules at the LCU, the launch control unit, a lot of red lights on it that shouldn't be there. And to make a long story short, we went up and worked on that thing in the snow and the ice one whole night. And of course the first thing, we just shut all the power off when we went up there. But we got it fixed. But that was probably as close as I've ever come to being in any sort of danger in that program.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: Uh-huh.

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: Or during the war.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: Now, we've actually got about a minute and a half left so I'm not going to try to push you for anything quickly, but I was just curious, was there any point in which you were in the nuclear weapons program when you really felt like we were getting close, that we might -- that there might actually be a war, that you might have to use --

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: Well, it would be that occasion.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: That occasion.

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: That occasion I think is as close as we had ever come to -- that I know of. Now, some of these people in the old mats of Curtis LeMay when he kept those bombers, B-52s in the air all the time with the nuclear weapons armed, and when I say armed, potentially armed, they arm them in the air.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: But they're not flying around with nuclear components in them. But anyhow, I think that -- he may have some stories to tell that would be closer to war than what I'm saying. But I hope that never happens. But I was very proud of my service in nuclear weapons and I was equally proud of my service as first sergeant, and I'd do every bit of it again.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: Right. That was going to be my last question. Is there anything you would change during the time you spent in the service?

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Michael Willie
sp.p: All right. Well, thank you for your time. You did a great job.

sp.speaker: Howard Finley Bolton
sp.p: Thank you.
